replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I have read the trip telemetry, the fare lines, the chat log and both advocates' submissions, and I rule as follows.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED, BUT NOT MATERIAL. On POL-RD-01 the distance is measured on the GPS trace, and the trace figure of 27.18 km (EV-GPS-00101) governs over the trip record's rounded 27.2 km (EV-TRIP-00101). Against the booked optimal of 21.0 km the excess is 6.18 km, or 29.4%. That clears both establishment tests (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation stands on this trip's own clean telemetry. It does NOT clear either materiality gate (more than 50% or more than 8.0 km), so it is a non-material deviation.

NO EXCULPATORY CLAUSE APPLIES. No traffic advisory exists for the AYE/MCE/ECP corridor in the trip window: EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0, and I record that impairment openly - the absence is itself citable and both advocates may rely on it. With no advisory there is no named road, no validity window and no alternative-route figure, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and none of the 6.18 km is exonerated. There was no rider-requested detour (every chat message carries waypoint_hint = null and no road is named, so POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test is undecidable and the clause is unavailable). There was no pickup or dropoff amendment (all POL-RD-05 fields are null), and this is a RYDE_X trip, not a pooled one, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The excess stands unreduced.

THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies (not POL-RD-11). Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0). Refund = charged_total 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of the charged total, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of $8.05, not the full $10.00 claimed - the optimal trip was never free, and $27.63 of the fare properly stands. The driver's in-app admission ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') is accepted as an honest account of a navigational error; it confirms the route error but does not change the arithmetic.

NO UPLIFT, NO REFERRAL, NO ESCALATION. Because the deviation is not material, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 812 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists - no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Nothing under POL-RD-09 to correct: the fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantries, carries optimal-route ERP of 0.0, and has no airport surcharge, so there is nothing to add on top. No driver compensation is due - the rider was billed 27.2 km, matching the 27.18 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (229 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not fire, and no mandatory escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 is present (identifiers match, timestamps agree, refund is below both SGD 150.00 and the charged total). Every deciding artifact - EV-GPS-00101, EV-TRIP-00101 and EV-FARE-00101 - carries weight 1.0, so my confidence is not capped below them. Profiles were used only as POL-GEN-01 permits, i.e., the citable 90-day counters for the POL-RD-06 test and nothing else.
